what_happened: The task description rules that the bottom PR of a stack targets the integration branch. With isolation off, each task's phase commits are already on that branch, so a review branch cut from the batch's cut point cannot be merged into it in general: in a three-task fixture, merging the first review branch into the integration branch conflicted on a file a later task had also edited, and only the full-stack tip merged cleanly, as a no-op. The landing record says the review ref is 'the thing merged' without naming what it merges into. Raised as a non-blocking user decision with a measured recommendation rather than filled by guessing.

milestone-review-handoff.sh prints '/please push <integration branch>' then '/merge'. /merge acts on the checked-out branch, refuses outright on main or master, hardcodes the remote name origin and the target main, and its prompt-time grant is minted for the checked-out branch only. In a repository whose integration branch is its default branch, the printed /merge refuses; on a feature integration branch it opens one PR of the whole branch, not a stack. A review branch that is never checked out cannot be submitted through /merge as it stands.

The landing task's interface to review submission was present and unambiguous on all three owed items (ref read, per-task proof instead of a range, not one commit per task), and its blob-overlay recipe reproduced in a fresh fixture on the first attempt: three stacked review branches, one commit each, with HEAD, the index and the working tree byte-identical before and after. The same fixture showed that git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base restacks a child after its parent is squash-merged with a tree equal to a full rebuild, and unlike the overlay it keeps a foreign mainline edit to the same file.

Plan authoring: suite_selection_select returns only the full-sweep sentinel for a script and suite a plan will create, since neither exists at authoring time, so a non-final phase editing only those two files cannot name a measured suite list in its Tier Justification; the plan carries the re-measurement as a Scope Hypothesis instead.

Plan authoring: the relayed review-base decision removed the only open design question; all three flagged description premises re-validated against live state (source_dir resolves in this repository, pr-prohibition rule and guard-git-push.sh present, landing contract section present in the decision record).

review-stack-prepare.sh's refusal path initially called 'exit CODE' from inside resolver functions whose output was captured via $(...) command substitution; exit inside a command-substitution subshell only terminates that subshell, so the refusal's exit code never reached the script's own exit status (silently exit 0). Fixed by refactoring every resolver to set a global variable and calling exit as a plain statement, never inside $(...).

Prior art (milestone-review-handoff.sh's resolve_integration_branch, batch-admission-lib.sh's declared-key reader pattern, test-milestone-review-handoff.sh's deployed-shape sandbox fixture convention and static-assertion grep idiom) transplanted directly into review-stack-prepare.sh and its suite, letting Phase 1 (script + 19-case suite + registration) complete in one pass with no rework beyond the exit-code bug.

Phase 1's Batch Gate Deferral scoped check (bash .claude/scripts/verify-touched.sh, no args) ran 139+98=237 suites and reported 3 failures, none involving review-stack-prepare.sh or test-review-stack-prepare.sh: 2 were pre-existing/expected baseline failures (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) and 1 'NEW' (test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh) flagged three OTHER sibling tasks' in-flight test files (test-lean-challenge-observe.sh, test-sapience-remember.sh, test-sapience-tag-pending.sh) missing suite-classification.data rows -- unrelated to this phase's own two correctly-registered files. Phase 1 verification is clean.
